If you have a filter selected, then the run now will be available unless it is still working on running filters already.I have lots of filter and lots of sorting of incoming mail occurs with them. I have not seen the run now remain unavailable for more than a minute after I click run now in years.

Things to consider generally and specifically.

When using IMAP moving messages can be exceedingly slow as each move involves multiple round trips to the mail server to complete the action. hen doing bulk filtering it can add up quickly. Especially if your internet connection upload is slow as most consumer ones are. Commercial/Business connections tend to symmetric. Consumer offerings are generally about 10% of the advertised download speed. If can make a difference.

Allowing an antivirus to scan in the profile folder can lead to significant slowdowns and on occasion data corruption. Especially if there re many targets messages that will be copied or moved to another folder. While the read part of the filter may only open the folder once. The write part may open and close the destination file multiple times. Each update can see an antivirus scan of the file initiated. SAO moving say 50 message to a new folder could see that destination open updated scanned and opened again 50 times. Make your life easier and make sure any antivirus that has on access scanning of the file system is not scanning in your Thunderbird profile folder.

Do not place the Thunderbird profile anywhere normally associated with document storage. Backups, access scanning and cloud syncing are all bad news for Thunderbird data.

To diagnose problems with Thunderbird, try one of the following:

  • Restart Thunderbird with add-ons disabled (Thunderbird troubleshooting Mode). On the Help menu, click on "Troubleshooting mode". If Thunderbird works like normal, there is an Add-on or Theme interfering with normal operations. You will need to re-enable add-ons one at a time until you locate the offender.
  • Restart the operating system in safe mode with Networking. This loads only the very basics needed to start your computer while enabling an Internet connection. Click on your operating system for instructions on how to start in safe mode: Windows 10, Windows 8, Windows 7, Windows Vista, Windows XP, OSX
If safe mode for the operating system fixes the issue, there's other software in your computer that's causing problems. Possibilities include but not limited to: AV scanning, virus/malware, background downloads such as program updates.

The first thing is to get the public keys from all your recipients. That is very difficult to do because few people have keys, few people care to make the effort to learn about encryption and get their own keys, and understanding encryption is difficult for many people.

If you want other people to encrypt messages to you, you will have to get your own public and private keys, give all your senders your public key, and ask them to encrypt their messages to you. That is also very difficult to do because, as I said, few people care to learn enough about encryption to do that and understanding encryption is difficult for many people.

Here is an excellent description of the issues involved in e-mail encryption. You may be able to decide better whether or not to use it after reading it. https://www.fastmail.com/blog/email-encryption/

Some people seem content when using an e-mail service provider that offers encryption such as Proton and Tuta. I don't know why they are content because the same challenges cited above stil exist unless all correspondents are also using an e-mail service provider that offers encryption.

content:
What is your operating system? I will assume Windows

What is your Anti-Virus, if any?

Do you use a VPN?

"Localhost" refers to your local computer. Normally Thunderbird interacts with the Internet directly. There should be no local proxy involved unless you intentionally use one.

This can often be caused by an Anti-Virus program inserting itself between the mail agent (Thunderbird) and the Internet in order to "helpfully" scan your emails. It could also be caused by malware doing the same thing for less "helpful" reasons.

Some things to try:

- Check the Thunderbird setting <Settings | General | Network & Disk Space | Connection> and click the "Settings" button. The default setting is "Use system proxy settings". A clue could be if "Manual proxy configuration" is something you don't recognize. Try temporarily changing it to "No proxy" and restart Thunderbird.

- Turn off your VPN, if you use one.

- Temporarily disable your AV or disable any of its options to scan your email.

- Restart Windows in Safe Mode with Networking. This temporarily disables the AV.

Please report your results.
